question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000, and no medical evidence is required.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.supports: The 60-day time limit (from leaving service, and only if cover is taken up before normal retirement age), the no-medical-evidence basis, and that cover is limited to the lower of the group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

citations.label: c12
citations.quote: Cover ends at the scheme's normal retirement age, or age 65 at the latest.
citations.supports: Normal retirement age is the point at which group cover ends, which is why the continuation option applies only to members who leave before that age.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: The documents describe a continuation option for group life cover only; they do not state a continuation option for group disability income or funeral cover.
The amount is the lower of the member's actual group cover and R5 000 000, so the member's own cover level decides the figure.

result.question: What waiting period applies to disability income Option B?
result.answer:
Under Option B of the Kestrel Group Disability Income Benefit, the waiting period is 6 months. So a member must complete a 6-month waiting period before the monthly income benefit becomes payable.

Option B pays 75% of monthly salary, with annual escalation of CPI capped at 6%, up to a maximum monthly benefit of R250 000. For comparison, Options A and C both have a 3-month waiting period.

One practical point for the caller: the claim should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period.

question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?

result.question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?
result.answer:
The documents do not give a premium rate per R1 000 of life cover. Kestrel's group life premiums are expressed as a percentage of the total annual salary bill of covered members, and the rate is guaranteed for 2 years from the scheme commencement or review date, after which it is reviewed based on scheme experience.

A scheme with 150 members falls in Band 3 (100 to 249 members). That band sets a group life free cover limit of R3 500 000 per member — it is not a premium rate. result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?
result.answer: Kestrel aims to make a decision on group life claims within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. So the clock only starts once every required document is in. Disability claims may take longer, because medical information may need to be obtained. (For comparison, funeral claims are paid within 48 hours of receiving complete documents.)
